## sc

Fire LLM agents at a repository

### Synopsis

Slop Cannon (sc) fires a crew of LLM agents at a git repository: a product
owner plans the work as beads (bd issues), engineers implement each bead in
its own worktree, and UX/QA/test reviewers loop feedback until every tester
is satisfied. Run it with a repo path and watch the TUI, or add -m to start
from a written brief.

  safety     PRs (on, the default) or straight to the default branch (off)
  cartridge  the CLI LLM subscription that gets used (blank until you add one)
  ammo       number of sub agents (minimum 3, default 10)
  vibes      stylistic choices communicated to all agents
  rules      rules communicated to all agents
  -m         start work with this brief; a bare repo path means full autopilot

### Usage

```
sc [flags] <repo-path>
sc [command]
```

### Examples

```
sc ./repo-path

sc ./repo-path -m "here's what I want done"

sc cartridge --add claude --model fable
sc cartridge --remove claude
sc cartridge --add animus
sc cartridge --add kimi --model 3
sc ammo 12
sc vibes --add vibes.md
sc rules --add rules.md
sc safety off
```

### Options

```
      --ammo N           override ammo for this run (N agents at once, minimum 3)
      --auto-merge       override auto_merge for this run: squash-merge the run's own pull requests once green (needs safety on)
      --cartridge NAME   fire cartridge NAME instead of the active one
      --dry-run          print the run this repository, config and flags add up to, without firing anything
      --force            start even though another run holds this repository's lock (only when you know it is gone)
      --global           read and write the global config only, not the repo config
      --headless         no TUI: render events as log lines (for CI and scripts)
  -h, --help             help for sc
      --json             print machine-readable JSON instead of text
  -m, --message BRIEF    start work with this BRIEF; without it the run is full autopilot
      --no-anim          disable the cannon animations in the TUI (also honours SC_NO_ANIM)
      --no-color         disable colour output (also honours NO_COLOR)
      --repo PATH        target repository PATH (default ".")
      --resume           continue the most recent run of this repository instead of starting a new one
      --review-prs       also review open pull requests sc did not create (needs gh and a remote) (default true)
      --run ID           with --resume, continue run ID instead of the most recent one
      --safety on|off    override safety for this run (on|off): on opens PRs, off merges to the default branch
  -v, --verbose          enable debug logging
```

## sc ammo

Set how many agents run at once (minimum 3, default 10)

### Synopsis

Set the ammo: how many agent subprocesses may be alive at once.

The minimum is 3 (one engineer, one tester, one product owner); the default
is 10. The value is written to the repo config when --repo (default: the
current directory) is inside a git repository, otherwise to the global
config; --global always writes the global config.

The allocation the value implies is printed: one product-owner slot, at most
max(1, floor((ammo-1)/4)) engineers in flight, and every remaining slot for
testers so each engineer can have three reviewers.

Without N the effective value and where it comes from is printed instead.

### Usage

```
sc ammo [N] [flags]
```

### Examples

```
sc ammo 12
sc --global ammo 6
sc ammo
```

### Options

```
  -h, --help   help for ammo
```

      --json        print machine-readable JSON instead of text
      --no-color    disable colour output (also honours NO_COLOR)
      --repo PATH   target repository PATH (default ".")
  -v, --verbose     enable debug logging
```

## sc cartridge

Add, remove, list, or switch the LLM CLI subscriptions

### Synopsis

A cartridge is an LLM CLI subscription sc can fire: the CLI to run and the
model to pass it. Cartridges are subscriptions, so they always live in the
global config, never in a repository (--global and --repo make no difference
here).

The first cartridge added becomes the active one; --use switches. Removing
the active cartridge promotes the next configured one, or leaves the cannon
without an active cartridge (a run refuses to start until one is added).
Re-adding a configured cartridge updates its model.

Supported: "claude" (Claude Code), "cursor" (Cursor Agent) and
"dandelion", the dandelion quota router, which fires Claude Code or Cursor
Agent on whichever account still has quota. Its --model is "high" (the
strongest model with quota) or "standard"; the router names the real model,
so roles.<role>.model is ignored for it. More cartridges are planned; any
other name is rejected. Without flags the configured cartridges are listed.

### Usage

```
sc cartridge [flags]
```

### Examples

```
sc cartridge --add claude --model fable
sc cartridge --add dandelion --model high
sc cartridge --remove claude
sc cartridge --add animus
sc cartridge --add kimi --model 3
sc cartridge --use claude
sc cartridge --list
```

### Options

```
      --add NAME      add cartridge NAME (or update its model); the first one added becomes active
  -h, --help          help for cartridge
      --list          list the configured cartridges (the default)
      --model M       model M to pass to the cartridge's CLI (with --add)
      --remove NAME   remove cartridge NAME
      --use NAME      make cartridge NAME the active one
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --global      read and write the global config only, not the repo config
      --json        print machine-readable JSON instead of text
      --no-color    disable colour output (also honours NO_COLOR)
      --repo PATH   target repository PATH (default ".")
  -v, --verbose     enable debug logging
```

## sc completion

Print a shell completion script (bash, zsh, or fish)

### Synopsis

Print a shell completion script for sc to stdout. Source it (or install it
where your shell looks for completions) and tab completion works for every
sc command and flag.

bash (needs bash-completion; bash 4 or newer):
  # once, for the current shell:
  source <(sc completion bash)
  # permanently:
  sc completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/sc                # Linux
  sc completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/sc  # macOS

zsh:
  # once, for the current shell:
  source <(sc completion zsh)
  # permanently (then start a new shell; add "autoload -U compinit; compinit"
  # to ~/.zshrc if completions are not enabled yet):
  sc completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_sc"

fish:
  # once, for the current shell:
  sc completion fish | source
  # permanently:
  sc completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/sc.fish

### Usage

```
sc completion bash|zsh|fish
```

### Examples

```
sc completion bash
sc completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_sc"
sc completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/sc.fish
```

### Options

```
  -h, --help              help for completion
      --no-descriptions   omit command descriptions from the completion script
```

```

## sc config

Show, locate, or edit the configuration files

### Synopsis

Inspect and edit the two configuration files.

sc reads the global config ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/slop-cannon/config.toml, by
default ~/.config/slop-cannon/config.toml) and the repo config
(<repo>/.slop-cannon/config.toml) and merges them over the built-in
defaults: flags beat the repo file, which beats the global file (D-03).
Cartridges live in the global file only.

Config subcommands write the repo file when --repo (default: the current
directory) is inside a git repository, otherwise the global file; --global
always picks the global file.

### Usage

```
sc config [flags]
sc config [command]
```

### Examples

```
sc config show
sc --json config show
sc config path
sc --global config edit
```

## sc config edit

Open the config file in $EDITOR

### Synopsis

Open the config file that config subcommands would write to (see sc config
path) in $EDITOR, falling back to $VISUAL. The file is created with the
current schema version when it does not exist yet. After the editor exits
the file is parsed and the merged configuration is validated, so a typo or
an invalid value is reported immediately with its line number; the file is
left as edited.

### Usage

```
sc config edit [flags]
```

### Options

## sc config show

Print the merged configuration with the source of every value

### Synopsis

Print the effective configuration: every key, its merged value, and the
layer that supplied it (default, global, repo, global+repo for the vibes and
rules lists that are unioned across files). The files consulted are listed
after the table; warnings such as cartridges found in a repo file are printed
to stderr. With --json the merged config, the sources, the file paths, the
warnings and the rows are printed as one object.

## sc doctor

Check that git, bd, dolt, gh, the cartridge CLIs and the repository are ready

### Synopsis

Check that everything a run needs is installed and configured:

  git        present and at least 2.30
  bd         present and at least 1.2.2 (the beads CLI with embedded Dolt)
  dolt       the beads project uses the embedded backend (warning in server
             mode, which sc has not been tested against; the standalone dolt
             CLI is irrelevant in embedded mode)
  beads      bd ping answers when the repo already has a .beads/ directory
  gh         present and authenticated (warning only; needed for safety-on
             gates and external PR review)
  cartridge  every configured cartridge CLI is on PATH (failure when the
             active one is missing)
  repo       --repo is a git repository with a clean working tree (warning)
  .gitignore ignores .env, so an agent cannot commit a credential (warning)
  .beads     present (warning: it is initialised on the first run)

Rows are pass, warn, or fail. The exit status is 1 when any row fails.

### Usage

```
sc doctor [flags]
```

### Options

```
  -h, --help   help for doctor
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --global      read and write the global config only, not the repo config

## sc logs

Tail the log of a run, an agent, or a bead

### Synopsis

Tail the logs of a run.

Without arguments it prints the orchestrator's own log (sc.log). With an
agent id it prints that agent's log; with a bead id it prints the log of
every agent that has worked on that bead, oldest agent first, each under a
header naming it.

With --follow it keeps printing as the logs grow, and waits for a log that
is not there yet: follow a bead the moment the run adopts it and the output
starts when its first agent spawns. Without --follow a bead that has no
agent log yet is an error, because a one-shot read has nothing to print.

Logs are read straight from the run directory, so this works on a finished
run, on a crashed one, and while another sc process is still firing —
nothing here writes anything. --run picks a run other than the most recent
one; sc status lists what a run has done.

### Usage

```
sc logs [AGENT-ID|BEAD-ID] [flags]
```

### Examples

```
sc logs
sc logs eng-sc-1-r1
sc logs sc-1
sc logs --repo ./repo-path --lines 200
sc logs sc-1 --follow
```

### Options

```
  -f, --follow    keep printing as the logs grow, waiting for a log that is not there yet (until interrupted)
  -h, --help      help for logs
  -n, --lines N   print the last N lines of each log (0 for all of it) (default 50)
      --run ID    read run ID instead of the most recent one
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --global      read and write the global config only, not the repo config
      --json        print machine-readable JSON instead of text
      --no-color    disable colour output (also honours NO_COLOR)
      --repo PATH   target repository PATH (default ".")
  -v, --verbose     enable debug logging
```

## sc resume

Continue the most recent run of a repository

### Synopsis

Continue the most recent run of a repository.

This is exactly "sc PATH --resume": the run keeps its id, its brief and the
configuration it was started with (a config file edited since does not
change it, and a note says so), its worktrees are reattached, stale leases
are recovered and the agents that were in flight are fired again.

PATH may be the repository root or any directory inside it; without it the
--repo directory (the current one by default) is used. --run ID continues
that run instead of the most recent one. --ammo, --safety and --cartridge
still override the frozen configuration for this invocation and say so.
There is nothing to resume in a repository sc has never run in.

### Usage

```
sc resume [PATH] [flags]
```

### Examples

```
sc resume
sc resume ./repo-path
sc resume --repo ./repo-path --headless
sc resume ./repo-path --run 20260924-214444-42c0 --safety off
```

### Options

```
      --ammo N           override ammo for this run (N agents at once, minimum 3)
      --auto-merge       override auto_merge for this run: squash-merge the run's own pull requests once green (needs safety on)
      --cartridge NAME   fire cartridge NAME instead of the active one
      --dry-run          print the run this repository, config and flags add up to, without firing anything
      --force            start even though another run holds this repository's lock (only when you know it is gone)
      --headless         no TUI: render events as log lines (for CI and scripts)
  -h, --help             help for resume
      --no-anim          disable the cannon animations in the TUI (also honours SC_NO_ANIM)
      --review-prs       also review open pull requests sc did not create (needs gh and a remote) (default true)
      --run ID           with --resume, continue run ID instead of the most recent one
      --safety on|off    override safety for this run (on|off): on opens PRs, off merges to the default branch
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --global      read and write the global config only, not the repo config

## sc rules

Manage the rule files every agent must follow

### Synopsis

Rules are files of hard constraints (what agents MUST and MUST NOT do:
branches to leave alone, commands never to run, APIs that are frozen) that
are appended to every agent prompt. Vibes (sc vibes) are taste; rules are
law.

--add FILE appends FILE (resolved from the current directory) to the rules
list of the repo config when --repo (default: the current directory) is
inside a git repository, otherwise of the global config; --global always
writes the global config. The file must exist, be UTF-8 text, and be at
most 64 KiB. Paths are stored relative to the config file's directory when
the file lives inside that tree, otherwise absolute, and a file listed
twice is kept once. --remove FILE drops it again from the same config file;
removing a file that is not listed is an error.

--list prints the effective rules list (global entries first, then repo
entries, in the order the agents see them) with where each entry comes from;
--show prints the concatenated content of those files. Both honour --global
by looking at the global config only. With no flags, --list is assumed.

### Usage

```
sc rules [--add FILE | --remove FILE | --list | --show] [flags]
```

### Examples

```
sc rules --add rules.md
sc --global rules --add ~/rules.md
sc rules --list
sc rules --show
sc rules --remove rules.md
```

### Options

```
      --add FILE      add FILE to the rules list (repeatable)
  -h, --help          help for rules
      --list          print the effective rules files and their sources
      --remove FILE   remove FILE from the rules list (repeatable)
      --show          print the concatenated content of the rules files
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --global      read and write the global config only, not the repo config
      --json        print machine-readable JSON instead of text
      --no-color    disable colour output (also honours NO_COLOR)
      --repo PATH   target repository PATH (default ".")
  -v, --verbose     enable debug logging
```

## sc run

Fire the cannon at a repository (same as `sc PATH`)

### Synopsis

Fire the cannon at a repository. PATH may be the repository root or any
directory inside it. Without -m the product owner researches the repository
and invents the work itself (autopilot, which never stops on its own); with
-m it decomposes your brief into beads and finishes when they are all
settled.

The run needs an active cartridge (sc cartridge --add claude --model M) and
PATH must be inside a git repository. --ammo, --safety and --cartridge
override the config files for this run only; everything else comes from the
effective configuration (sc config show). --resume continues the most
recent run recorded for the repository instead of starting a new one.

The TUI holds the finished run on screen until you press q, so the last
graph is there to read; --headless ends when the run does, and a reader
that closes early (sc run --headless | head) stops the run rather than
killing it. sc stop ends a run from another terminal.

This is the same as the bare form "sc PATH [flags]".

### Usage

```
sc run [PATH] [flags]
```

### Examples

```
sc ./repo-path
sc ./repo-path -m "here's what I want done"
sc run ./repo-path --headless --safety off --ammo 6
sc ./repo-path --resume
```

### Options

```
      --ammo N           override ammo for this run (N agents at once, minimum 3)
      --auto-merge       override auto_merge for this run: squash-merge the run's own pull requests once green (needs safety on)
      --cartridge NAME   fire cartridge NAME instead of the active one
      --dry-run          print the run this repository, config and flags add up to, without firing anything
      --force            start even though another run holds this repository's lock (only when you know it is gone)
      --headless         no TUI: render events as log lines (for CI and scripts)
  -h, --help             help for run
  -m, --message BRIEF    start work with this BRIEF; without it the run is full autopilot
      --no-anim          disable the cannon animations in the TUI (also honours SC_NO_ANIM)
      --resume           continue the most recent run of this repository instead of starting a new one
      --review-prs       also review open pull requests sc did not create (needs gh and a remote) (default true)
      --run ID           with --resume, continue run ID instead of the most recent one
      --safety on|off    override safety for this run (on|off): on opens PRs, off merges to the default branch

## sc safety

Open PRs (on, the default) or merge straight to the default branch (off)

### Synopsis

Set the safety switch (D-10).

  on   finished beads are pushed to an sc/<bead-id>-<slug> branch and opened
       as a pull request for a human to merge; the default branch is never
       touched. This is the default.
  off  finished beads are rebased onto the default branch, the check command
       is run, then they are fast-forward merged and pushed when a remote
       exists.

true/false, yes/no and 1/0 are accepted as well. The value is written to the
repo config when --repo (default: the current directory) is inside a git
repository, otherwise to the global config; --global always writes the
global config.

Without a value the effective setting and where it comes from is printed
instead.

### Usage

```
sc safety [on|off] [flags]
```

### Examples

```
sc safety off
sc --global safety on
sc safety
```

### Options

```
  -h, --help   help for safety
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --global      read and write the global config only, not the repo config
      --json        print machine-readable JSON instead of text
      --no-color    disable colour output (also honours NO_COLOR)
      --repo PATH   target repository PATH (default ".")
  -v, --verbose     enable debug logging
```

## sc status

Show the state of a run, or one bead's timeline

### Synopsis

Report what a run did and is doing.

Without arguments it describes the most recent run recorded for the
repository (--run ID picks another): its phase, how its beads are spread
across the workflow states, what it delivered — pull requests, merges, and
the reviews it posted on pull requests it did not open — which agents are
live, and the last few events.
Everything comes from the run directory — state.json and events.jsonl — so
it also works after a crash and while another process holds the run.

The bead states are then reconciled with bd, so a bead a human closed or
reopened by hand is reported as it stands rather than as the run last left
it; --live=false skips that and reports the run log alone, which is also
what happens when the repository has no beads database or bd is not
installed.

With a bead id it prints that bead's timeline from beads: creation, the
claim, every structured message sc recorded (verdicts, responses,
arbitrations, deliveries) and where the bead stands now. This form needs bd
on PATH and a beads database in the repository.

### Usage

```
sc status [BEAD-ID] [flags]
```

### Examples

```
sc status
sc status --repo ./repo-path
sc status --run 20260902-010203-abcd --events 25
sc status sc-1a2b
sc status --json
```

### Options

```
      --events N   how many recent events to print (N, 0 for none) (default 10)

## sc stop

Stop the run going in a repository

### Synopsis

Stop the run going in a repository, from anywhere.

PATH may be the repository root or any directory inside it; without it the
--repo directory (the current one by default) is used.

It reads the repository's run lock, interrupts the sc process holding it —
the same graceful stop Ctrl-C asks for, so the agents in flight finish,
their leases are released and the worktrees are tidied — and waits for the
run to end. --now interrupts twice, which kills the agents where they
stand; --wait 0 returns as soon as the interrupt is delivered.

A run on another machine (a state directory on a shared file system) cannot
be signalled from here, and neither can a run that has already gone. Both
are reported rather than guessed at. Use sc status to see the run first.

### Usage

```
sc stop [PATH] [flags]
```

### Examples

```
sc stop
sc stop ./repo-path
sc stop --now
sc stop --wait 0
```

### Options

```
  -h, --help            help for stop
      --now             stop immediately: interrupt twice, so the agents are killed rather than finished
      --wait DURATION   wait up to DURATION for the run to finish (0 returns as soon as it is asked to stop) (default 2m0s)
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --global      read and write the global config only, not the repo config
      --json        print machine-readable JSON instead of text
      --no-color    disable colour output (also honours NO_COLOR)
      --repo PATH   target repository PATH (default ".")
  -v, --verbose     enable debug logging
```

## sc vibes

Manage the style files every agent is given

### Synopsis

Vibes are files of stylistic preferences (tone, naming, formatting, the
libraries you like) that are appended to every agent prompt as soft
guidance. Rules (sc rules) are the hard constraints; vibes are taste.

--add FILE appends FILE (resolved from the current directory) to the vibes
list of the repo config when --repo (default: the current directory) is
inside a git repository, otherwise of the global config; --global always
writes the global config. The file must exist, be UTF-8 text, and be at
most 64 KiB. Paths are stored relative to the config file's directory when
the file lives inside that tree, otherwise absolute, and a file listed
twice is kept once. --remove FILE drops it again from the same config file;
removing a file that is not listed is an error.

--list prints the effective vibes list (global entries first, then repo
entries, in the order the agents see them) with where each entry comes from;
--show prints the concatenated content of those files. Both honour --global
by looking at the global config only. With no flags, --list is assumed.

### Usage

```
sc vibes [--add FILE | --remove FILE | --list | --show] [flags]
```

### Examples

```
sc vibes --add vibes.md
sc --global vibes --add ~/vibes.md
sc vibes --list
sc vibes --show
sc vibes --remove vibes.md
```

### Options

```
      --add FILE      add FILE to the vibes list (repeatable)
  -h, --help          help for vibes
      --list          print the effective vibes files and their sources
      --remove FILE   remove FILE from the vibes list (repeatable)
      --show          print the concatenated content of the vibes files
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --global      read and write the global config only, not the repo config
      --json        print machine-readable JSON instead of text
      --no-color    disable colour output (also honours NO_COLOR)
      --repo PATH   target repository PATH (default ".")
  -v, --verbose     enable debug logging
```

## sc watch

Open the TUI on a run that is already firing

### Synopsis

Open the run TUI on a run that is already firing, from any terminal.

PATH may be the repository root or any directory inside it; without it the
--repo directory (the current one by default) is used. The most recent run
is watched unless --run names another.

It is the same TUI sc run draws: the bead graph, what every agent is
working on, the review rounds and verdicts, the pull requests, and the log.
It starts with everything the run has done so far and then follows it live,
so it is how a run fired with --headless, from a script, or in a terminal
that has since closed is watched.

Watching only reads the run's event log. The run controls are not offered,
and q leaves the TUI while the run keeps firing; use sc stop to stop it. A
run that has already finished is shown as it ended.

### Usage

```
sc watch [PATH] [flags]
```

### Examples

```
sc watch
sc watch ./repo-path
sc watch --run 20260924-214444-42c0
sc watch --no-anim
```

### Options

```
      --alt-screen   draw on the alternate screen buffer (default true)
  -h, --help         help for watch
      --no-anim      disable the cannon animations (also honours SC_NO_ANIM)
      --run ID       watch run ID instead of the most recent one
```

  -v, --verbose     enable debug logging
